lime-kiln.title: A view from Lime Kiln
lime-kiln.lead: Stand on the west side of San Juan Island. What nearby water has modeled viewing support—and how do distance, terrain and trees change the answer?
lime-kiln.text:
[Lime Kiln Point State Park](https://parks.wa.gov/find-parks/state-parks/lime-kiln-point-state-park)
is on San Juan Island's rocky western coast. Here, its lighthouse anchors an end-to-end reading
of the model: locate the source, compare four weights, see the shoreline, then inspect the exact records.
No installation is needed. For the ideas behind the maps, start with [How it works](understand/index.md).
lime-kiln.intro:
The diamond marks the lighthouse at approximately **48.5158° N, 123.1525° W**. Its native R7
cell is `{{lime_source}}`. Orange shading shows the model's active land within that cell;
the {{lime_observers}} brown dots are its retained regional observer samples (some overlap at this map scale). The source cell includes land beyond the park.
**These are area-level results for the cell containing Lime Kiln, not a calculation from the
lighthouse railing or from the photograph's camera position.**
lime-kiln.center_note: The source center is marked separately from the lighthouse, about 1.1 km southeast of it.

everett.name: Everett port area
everett.title: A view from Everett
everett.lead: Look across the working waterfront of Everett. How do distance, low coastal terrain and vegetation shape modeled support over Port Gardner and Possession Sound?
everett.text:
An urban waterfront offers a different setting from Lime Kiln: marinas, developed shore and nearby lowlands. The example uses the land part of a mixed coastal cell near the port; it does not represent a particular pier or viewing platform.

No installation is needed. For the ideas behind the maps, start with [How it works](understand/index.md).
everett.center_note: The diamond locates the selected source cell center; it is not a camera position or an additional modeled observer.
everett.selection_note: The table selects the highest combined score among this source's **non-self** target pairs:
everett.result_note: The terrain and canopy inputs describe a developed waterfront. Buildings, cranes, vessels and fences in the photographs are outside the obstruction model. Use the photographs to identify features that can change the view on site.
everett.intro: The diamond locates the center of native R7 source cell `{{lime_source}}`, approximately **48.0151° N, 122.2236° W**. Orange shading shows its retained active land; the {{lime_observers}} brown dots are the regional observer samples. **These are area-level results, not a calculation from a photograph's camera or a particular platform.**

everett.shore_reading: The marina view looks across boats and developed shore. The waterfront photograph shows nearer structures and changing sightlines. Ground and canopy weights cannot certify a clear line past a building, crane or moored vessel.

larrabee.name: Larrabee inland
larrabee.title: A view from the Larrabee woods
larrabee.lead: Move a little inland from the wooded coast of Larrabee State Park. Nearby water can have strong distance support while trees remove the modeled sightlines.
larrabee.text:
This example selects an inland cell in the Larrabee / Chuckanut landscape, rather than the beach. The photographs show the wider park setting, not verified camera positions in the selected cell. Compare its canopy effect with the coastal Lime Kiln and Everett examples.

No installation is needed. For the ideas behind the maps, start with [How it works](understand/index.md).
larrabee.center_note: The diamond locates the selected source cell center; it is not a camera position or an additional modeled observer.
larrabee.selection_note: All combined scores are zero. To show why, the table selects the **non-self pair with the highest terrain weight**:
larrabee.result_note: Terrain alone gives positive support to **{{terrain_positive}} targets**. With canopy included, all **{{lime_count}} candidate targets** have zero combined support for the sampled inland viewpoints. Compare the terrain and combined maps to see the change.
larrabee.intro: The diamond locates the center of native R7 source cell `{{lime_source}}`, approximately **48.6601° N, 122.4645° W**. Orange shading shows its retained active land; the {{lime_observers}} brown dots are the regional observer samples. **These are area-level results, not a calculation from a photograph's camera or a particular platform.**
